patterns: Language modules live in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/<lang>.rs with SPDX header

extract_inheritance handler walks node tree to find extends/implements clauses and returns Vec<String> with 'extends X' / 'implements Y' format

Query syntax: captures with @name, field access with field: (node_type), node kind matching with (kind_name ...)

approaches.name: Approach A: Minimal PHP handler with function/class/interface/trait/enum extraction
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY matching function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration; CALL_QUERY for method_invocation and function_call_expression; REFERENCE_QUERY for qualified_name; IMPORT_QUERY for namespace_use_declaration; DEFUSE_QUERY for local variable and assignment tracking. Implement extract_inheritance to walk base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire in mod.rs and lang.rs. Add unit tests for query compilation and inheritance extraction. Add integration test for .php file analysis.
pros: Follows established pattern from Swift/Java/Go integrations
Minimal scope: only required queries and handlers
Clear inheritance extraction via child node traversal
Straightforward testing: unit tests in php.rs, integration test in tests/integration_tests.rs
cons: Requires careful grammar inspection to identify correct node kinds and field names
base_clause/class_interface_clause are children, not fields, so extraction differs from Java's field-based approach
HTML-embedded PHP requires testing with mixed <?php ... ?> blocks to verify zero ERROR nodes

approaches.name: Approach B: Full-featured PHP handler with property/constant extraction
approaches.description: Extend Approach A to include property_declaration and const_declaration in ELEMENT_QUERY; add REFERENCE_QUERY for qualified_name and variable_name; add DEFUSE_QUERY tracking for property assignments. Implement handlers for extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type (currently unused but future-proofing). Add comprehensive tests covering all declaration kinds.
pros: Future-proof for potential handler reactivation (e.g., if #1807 is revisited)
More complete symbol extraction for property/constant analysis
cons: Out of scope per issue (properties and constants explicitly excluded)
Adds complexity without current consumer demand
Requires additional testing and maintenance burden
May introduce false positives if property extraction is incomplete

approaches.name: Approach C: PHP handler with DEFUSE_QUERY and local-scope tracking
approaches.description: Approach A plus a comprehensive DEFUSE_QUERY covering local_variable_declaration, assignment_expression, update_expression, and identifier reads. Implement fine-grained definition/use tracking for data-flow analysis. Add tests verifying DEFUSE_QUERY matches local declarations, assignments, and reads in nested scopes.
pros: Enables data-flow analysis and definition-use chains
DEFUSE_QUERY is required per acceptance criteria (though currently optional for some languages)
Follows Java/Go/Python pattern of comprehensive defuse tracking
Supports future refactoring and impact analysis tools
cons: Requires careful query design to avoid over-capturing or missing scopes
Testing complexity: must verify correct capture of local vs. global identifiers
PHP's dynamic scoping and variable variables make defuse tracking ambiguous

recommendation: Approach A (Minimal PHP handler with function/class/interface/trait/enum extraction). It directly addresses the issue scope, follows the established Swift/Java pattern, and keeps complexity manageable. The DEFUSE_QUERY is required per acceptance criteria and is included in Approach A. The key differentiator from Java is that PHP uses base_clause and class_interface_clause as child nodes rather than fields, which the extract_inheritance handler must navigate carefully. Testing the HTML-embedded PHP edge case (<?php ... ?> mixed with HTML) is critical to verify zero ERROR nodes.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
(
  (function_definition
    name: (name) @function_name) @function
  (method_declaration
    name: (name) @method_name) @function
  (class_declaration
    name: (name) @class_name) @class
  (interface_declaration
    name: (name) @interface_name) @class
  (trait_declaration
    name: (name) @trait_name) @class
  (enum_declaration
    name: (name) @enum_name) @class
)
inheritance_walk_citation: The PHP grammar stores inheritance information as child nodes of class_declaration, not as fields. To extract inheritance: (1) iterate child nodes of class_declaration using node.child(i); (2) for each child with kind() == 'base_clause', extract the name child node and prepend 'extends '; (3) for each child with kind() == 'class_interface_clause', iterate its name children and prepend 'implements ' to each. The base_clause contains a single name (the parent class); class_interface_clause contains comma-separated names (interfaces). This pattern is documented in tree-sitter-php's common/define-grammar.js: base_clause is defined as seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)) and class_interface_clause as seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)).
